question.prompt:
A solid is built from small cubes: the bottom layer has 2 rows and 2 columns, totaling 4 small cubes, and the second layer has only 1 small cube placed at one corner. How many small squares can be seen from above?

[Figure 1](figures/cnm_051_q3_question_en.svg)

solutions.explanation: The five cubes occupy four vertical columns. From above, each column contributes one visible top square. The upper cube is visible and hides the top face of the lower cube directly beneath it. Therefore there are \(4\) visible squares.
solutions.title: Count the vertical columns
